reviews.replacement: Choose a specific course of action intended for the next 30 minutes, then cast tokens or bones. The omen indicates good results (Weal), bad results (Woe), or both (Weal and Woe); no omen means no strong result either way. It provides no details or explanation. Casting again before a rest risks a random false reading.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Remaining descriptive overlap: The rewrite still uses Weal/Woe and their combined omen categories. The sentences are rephrased, but that was the original descriptive concern. Keep deliberately with an attribution decision, or replace the presentation if independence is the goal. Timing is excluded.

reviews.replacement: On a failed WIS save, the humanoid becomes charmed and considers you a friendly acquaintance. Harming it ends the effect; otherwise, the charm lasts for the spell’s duration. The humanoid has advantage on this save when fighting you or any of your allies.

Flora or Fauna:  Choose how nature transforms you. 

Fauna: Take an animal form to increase your speed by 10ft, gain advantage on STR-based attacks, and deal an extra 3d8 force damage on melee hits; or...

Flora: Take a rooted form that creates grasping roots extending 15ft around you.  Ensnares enemies (save vs. STR), grants allies within that area advantage against fear, and lets your ranged attacks ignore cover.  Caster is rooted in place for the duration.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Reference conflict: The chosen Fauna rewrite deals +3d8 force, but the dice field still says +1d6. Flora adds a STR save, restraint and a rooted caster, while the save field is N/A. Preserve the rewrite choice and reconcile these reference fields when implementing.

reviews.replacement: While the spell lasts, speech you hear in any language is intelligible to you at a literal level. Writing in any language is likewise intelligible, but only while you touch the surface bearing it. Ciphers, secret codes, and non-linguistic symbols remain undecoded. This understanding grants no ability to speak or write the language.
Create up to six fist-sized points of light (or combine them into one vaguely humanoid glow) within range and move them as a bonus action; each sheds dim light in a 10ft radius.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Reference conflict: The rewrite creates up to six lights; the targets field still allows four. The humanoid-combination option also remains, although the original torch-sized-light wording is gone.

reviews.replacement: Make an offering and perform a ritual to receive your deity’s truthful answer to ONE question. Choose a particular objective, occurrence, or undertaking expected within 7 days. The response takes the form of an omen, a brief phrase, or an enigmatic rhyme, revealing the future as it currently stands rather than hypothetical outcomes. Casting again before a rest risks a random false reading.
You are fluent in 'Druidic', the secret language of druids.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Remaining phrase overlap: The revised sentence still contains the six-word sequence Druidic, the secret language of druids in both SRDs. This is a short definition, not evidence by itself of infringement. Record a deliberate keep/attribution decision or rephrase if desired.

reviews.replacement: A 10' diameter pillar of holy fire crashes down from above; each creature in it makes a DEX save against 4d6 fire + 4d6 radiant (half on a success).
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Reference conflict: The rewrite specifies a 10-foot diameter, while the targets field specifies a 10-foot radius and 40-foot height. Choose the intended footprint before implementation; these are different areas.

reviews.replacement: The target envisions their own demise. The target must make a WIS save or take 1d8 necrotic — 1d12 if it is already below its hit point maximum.
Innate fey heritage: cast Charm Person once per day without a spell slot.
Warded creatures are completely undetectable to the undead. Mindless undead are utterly blind to you; intelligent ones save or lose you. The ward breaks on any warded creature that attacks.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Internal contradiction: The opening promises complete undetectability, but the next sentence allows intelligent undead a save. Qualify the opening so it does not overrule that exception. The original sensory wording is removed; remaining parallels mostly describe the same rules.

reviews.replacement: Handle an object through the casting to learn whether it is magical, what its properties are and how to use them. Cast on a creature, learn what spells or curses currently affect it (if any).
Even the slightest natural phenomenon provides enough cover for you to hide.  Leaves, snow, fog, even heavy rain all count.
A shockwave of necrotic energy explodes outward from the caster; every living creature inside takes 8d6 necrotic, CON for half.
Weave shadows into a blade of absolute darkness (2d8 psychic, finesse, thrown 20/60); you have advantage on attacks with it in dim light or darkness.
Create a 20ft sphere of absolute silence. Creatures inside cannot cast spells with verbal components; all sonic attacks including thunder damage are negated there.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Rule clarification: The rewrite says a 20ft sphere without specifying radius or diameter; the targets field says 20ft radius. It also expands negation from thunder damage to all sonic attacks. Preserve the choice, but make the intended area and scope explicit.

reviews.replacement: Communicate with animals. They can share what they have sensed recently, but are limited by animal intelligence and perspective.  Just because they CAN communicate back, doesn't mean they WILL.  The spell does not affect their disposition towards the caster.

Raise the countryside: conscript 5d10 locals into an army under your command — each soldier is level 2d6, armed appropriately to their station, and they fight with discipline borrowed from you for as long as you lead them. You may keep one such army at a time; raising a new one disbands the old.

Magically seal a closable object: it is locked and barred to all but those you designate at casting (you may also set a password that suppresses the seal for 1 minute when spoken within 5ft). Knock suppresses it for 10 minutes; breaking or picking it is 10 harder than normal.
Life-preserving radiance surrounds you. Allies in the aura resist necrotic damage and their maximum HP cannot be reduced; any ally at 0 HP that starts its turn in the aura wakes with 1 HP.
The target bleeds from every orifice, taking 1d4 necrotic at the start of each of its turns for 1d10 turns or until you cancel it.
The target makes a CON save or is blinded for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.
A melee weapon attack sheathed in thunder; if the target willingly moves before the end of your next turn, it takes 1d8 thunder.
A ghostly hand (ranged spell attack); 1d8 necrotic and the target cannot regain HP until the start of your next turn. Undead also have disadvantage on attacks against you until then.
A blast of killing frost pours from your hands; every creature within the cone makes a CON save against 8d8 cold. Creatures slain by it freeze where they stand, rimed statues until they thaw.
Affected creatures lose track of friend, foe and intent: each turn one wanders, one attacks whatever is nearest, one stands babbling. A creature may repeat the save at the end of each of its turns.
Automatically negate a spell of 3rd tier or lower. For a higher-tier spell, make a spellcasting ability check (DC 10 + that spell's tier) to interrupt it.  Requires line of sight to the caster.
Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a bonus action on each of your turns.
Touch a creature to restore 1d8 + your spellcasting modifier HP. No effect on undead or constructs.

A ward against the grave. Protects the target from dropping to 0 or less HP, instead it drops to 1 and the ward burns out; an effect that would kill outright without dealing damage is negated instead, spending the ward.

Sense magic within 30ft; as an action, see a faint aura around a visible magical creature or object and learn its tradition. Blocked by 1ft of stone, 1in of metal, or 3ft of wood. It DETECTS only — learning an item's specific properties is Identify.
Sense the location of any undead, fiend, or celestial within 60ft, and any consecrated or desecrated place, until the end of your next turn.

Seize a beast's mind. It obeys your commands — even self-destructive ones — and you can perceive through its senses by concentrating. Each time it takes damage it re-saves, and success shakes it free.
A creature (not undead or construct) makes a WIS save or is frightened of you, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.
A ranged spell attack hurling a 4-inch orb of acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder (you choose) for 3d8.
Double your proficiency bonus on checks with a chosen skill you are proficient in (fixed when the expertise was gained — e.g. Stealth, Deception, Thieves' Tools).
One extra attack per round.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Rule clarification: One extra attack per round does not say which action grants it or whether it stacks with Double Attack. The previous wording tied two attacks to taking the attack action. This is a rules change to confirm, not a spelling correction.

reviews.replacement: Each creature in the cube that fails a DEX save is outlined in light: attacks against it have advantage and it cannot benefit from invisibility.

Each creature in the cone sees its own worst thing; on a failed WIS save it drops what it holds and flees by the fastest route for as long as it can see you. It may repeat the save at the end of each of its turns.
A reaction when you or nearby creatures fall: up to five falling creatures descend 60ft per round and take no damage when landing.
Advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep.

A soundless burst of white light at a creature's eye level; on a failed CON save it is blinded until the end of its next turn. Useless against a creature that cannot see, and it plainly announces that magic was cast.
Gain 1d4+4 temporary hit points for the duration.
The target gains a flying speed of 60ft for the duration.

A faintly shimmering sphere surrounds you. No spell of tier 5 or lower cast from outside can affect anything within it — the magic simply fails at the boundary. Creatures and objects pass freely; the globe does not move with you.
Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.
A chill of the grave; the target makes a CON save or has disadvantage on its next attack roll.
Slick grease coats the ground. A creature in the area when it appears, or entering it, makes a DEX save or falls prone; the area is difficult ground while it lasts. It burns if set alight.
Once before the spell ends, the target adds 1d4 to one ability check of its choice.
A ranged spell attack; 2d6 radiant on a hit, and the next attack roll against that target before the end of your next turn has advantage.
A bonus action: one creature you can see regains 1d4 + your spellcasting modifier HP. No effect on undead or constructs.
As a reaction to taking damage from an enemy you can see, wreathe it in hellish flame; it takes 2d10 fire, halved on a successful DEX save.

A humanoid you can see must make a WIS save or be paralyzed. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Humanoids only — not beasts, undead, or monstrosities.

Mark one creature you can see. Your weapon attacks against THAT target deal +1d6 damage, and you have advantage to track it. EXCLUSIVE: only one Hunter's Mark can exist at a time — casting it reassigns to the new target. The mark fades upon the target's death.

Fist-sized hailstones hammer down through everything in the cylinder; each creature makes a DEX save, taking 4d6 bludgeoning + 4d6 cold (half on a success). The ground is ice-slicked, difficult terrain until the end of your next turn.
Your next successful melee attack causes an additional 3d10 necrotic damage.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Rule clarification: The rewrite adds damage to the next successful melee attack rather than making an immediate melee spell attack. Its duration is still instantaneous. Specify how long the charge lasts and whether it applies to weapon attacks before implementation.

reviews.replacement: A CHA check to terrify one creature. On a success it is shaken (-2 to all rolls) until it can no longer see you or the scene ends.
A creature you touch becomes invisible until it attacks, casts a spell, or the spell ends. Anything it is wearing or carrying is invisible too.
Advantage on Perception checks that rely on sight, hearing, or smell.
Draw from a healing pool of 5 × your level: touch to restore HP, or spend 5 points to cure one disease or neutralize one poison. Cannot harm undead.
A nonmagical weapon becomes a magic weapon with +1 to attack and damage rolls for the duration.
A wave of restorative energy washes over the point you choose; up to six creatures of your choice within it each regain 3d8 + your casting modifier HP. Undead and constructs are untouched.

Whisper a short message to one creature within range that only it hears; it may whisper a one-line reply only you hear. Requires line of sight. Does NOT reach beyond 120ft — it is not telepathy or long-distance sending.
A bonus action: teleport up to 30ft to an unoccupied space you can see. Line of sight required — you cannot step through a wall you can't see past.
A 5ft beam of moonlight; a creature that enters it or starts its turn there takes 2d10 radiant (CON save half). You may move the beam 60ft each turn.
Advantage on saving throws against poison, and resistance (half damage) to poison.
Your next melee hit expends a slot to deal +2d8 radiant (more with a higher slot; +1d8 extra against undead or fiends).
A ray of enervation (ranged spell attack); the target deals only half damage with STR-based weapon attacks until the spell ends (CON save each turn to end it early).
A ranged spell attack; 1d8 cold on a hit and the target's speed drops by 10ft until the start of your next turn.
A ray of sickly energy (ranged spell attack); 1d8 necrotic and, on a failed CON save, the target is poisoned until the end of your next turn.
Attack with advantage this turn; in exchange, attacks against you have advantage until your next turn.
A reaction when you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage: gain resistance to that type until your next turn, and your next melee hit deals +1d6 of it.
Restores a dead creature to life with its body intact, so long as the soul consents. A century in the grave is not too long.
The greater Bleed: the target festers with necrotic sores, taking 1d6 necrotic at the start of each of its turns for 1d10 turns or until cancelled.
Radiant light falls on a creature you can see; it makes a DEX save or takes 1d8 radiant.  Cover is ignored.

Ward one creature: an enemy that tries to attack or target it must first make a WIS save or be forced to pick a new target, or the attack is lost. No protection against area effects, and the ward ends immediately if the warded creature in any way attacks.
From an area of dim light or darkness, teleport up to 30ft to another area of dim light or darkness in line of sight.
A reaction (cast when hit or targeted by Magic Missile): +5 AC until the start of your next turn, INCLUDING against the triggering attack, and negates Magic Missile.
Reduce all incoming damage by 3 until the start of your next turn. Requires a shield or braced stance.

On a failed WIS save a creature's speed halves, it takes a penalty to AC and DEX saves, and it can take only one action or one bonus action on its turn. It may repeat the save at the end of each of its turns.

Name a creature you can see and your god strikes it directly: a single blow equal to 95% of the hit points it has left, delivered in your deity's own idiom — a thunderclap, ghostly tentacles from the deep; the GM chooses the manifestation. It is never a killing blow: whatever it hits is left at death's door, and what happens next is up to you.
Stabilize a creature at 0 HP (it no longer needs death saves). No effect on undead or constructs.
Divine wrath rides your weapon. Your next hit deals +4d6 psychic, and the target makes a WIS save or reels — disadvantage on attacks and checks, and no reactions, until the end of its next turn.

The caster steals the target's voice.  While active, the caster's voice is indistinguishable from that of the target, and the target is left entirely unable to speak.  A successful Constitution save reduces the effect to a single utterance of the caster.
Nobody breaks where you stand. Allies who can see or hear you cannot be routed, frightened or panicked, and the wounded among them keep their feet as long as you keep yours.
The caster grants a run speed increase to themselves and their allies for the duration.  Those affected can run non-stop at double their normal speed for the duration of the spell.
A vine lashes out (melee spell attack at range); 1d6 piercing and, if the target is equal in size or smaller to the caster, you pull it up to 10ft toward you.
Channel Divinity: each undead within 30ft that fails a WIS save must spend its turns fleeing you and cannot willingly move closer, for 1 minute or until it takes damage.
If an attack hits you and you can see the attacker, you may spend your reaction to take half the damage from that attack. You have one reaction per round.

Raise a dense barrier of sharp, thorn-covered vines, up to 20 feet in length, 10 feet in height and 3 feet thick. An opponent can break through by succeeding on a STR saving throw; failure leaves them restrained until they succeed on the save or are released. Contact with the vines deals 2d6 damage, which the saving throw does not reduce.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Duplicate name: There is another capability keyed wall of thorns (one space). This two-space entry is 2d6/STR/4 hours; the other is 7d8/DEX/concentration. They must remain separate until you choose which to keep or give them distinct names. Removing the extra space would create a collision. This entry also targets self despite describing a wall at range.

reviews.replacement: While below half your maximum HP, your melee attacks deal an extra 1d4 damage.
Your touch rots living flesh: 2d8 necrotic and the target ages 1d10 years. What you rot stays rotted — wounds you deal cannot be magically healed until the next dawn.
WIS save or cursed — choose: disadvantage on one ability's checks and saves, OR vulnerability to one damage type, OR the target wastes its action on a roll of 1-4.
Accelerates the target's age by 2d10 years (CON for half). Pushed beyond its natural span, the body begins to fail.
Bolster up to three creatures: their hit point maximum AND current HP each increase by 5 for 8 hours.

Your own soul rides in a prepared vessel: the first time you die, you wake beside it a day later and the vessel shatters. Crafting a new anchor takes a month. This is the apprenticeship for what waits at level 17.
The moon shows you older beasts: forms long extinct — cave bears the size of carts, wolves from the first winters. Your shapes now frighten as they fight.
Your marked quarry is already dead and its body just hasn't heard: your attacks against it crit on 18–20, it cannot hide from you, and your allies strike it harder for knowing you're on it.
Once per round, step into a living tree and out of another of the same kind within 500ft — oak into oak, pine into pine. You know the location of every such tree in range while the spell lasts.
A ranged spell attack (INT vs AC); 1d8 force on a hit. The sorcerer's reliable at-will strike.
A shimmer of force absorbs the next 5 damage you take, then dissipates. Raised as a reaction.
You see magic as plainly as light. Every enchantment, ward, curse and active spell declares itself; every illusion shows its brushstrokes; every disguised face shows the one beneath.

Your Mage Hand grown to full strength and reach: invisible, it can carry a person's weight, force a stuck door, wield a weapon at your direction, or throttle. It is as strong as you are and can be attacked only by dispelling.
Waves of skeletons crash against the enemy, 25 at a time. As skeletons fall, new ones rise and join the fight. It continues until your concentration breaks.
The guilty do not get to leave: once per scene, halt a fleeing foe where it stands — teleport, wings or terror avail it nothing for one full round.
The caster manifests as the scythed icon of Death itself. Foes who behold it are petrified, one foe per round must save vs death or be reaped and die.

Take on the aspect of an undead creature appropriate to your power — a ghoul's paralyzing claws, a wraith's incorporeal drift, a mummy's dreadful gaze — gaining that creature's signature trait while the aspect holds.
A silver-grey horse of solid starlight forms and will carry you tirelessly at speed, over ground a real horse would refuse. It vanishes if it takes any damage, and cannot fight.
Allies within 10ft cannot be frightened while you stand.
You and every ally within 10ft add your CHA modifier to all saving throws while you stand.
For the duration, use a bonus action to heal one creature within 30ft for 2d6.

The target is hurled into a harmless demiplane and simply ceases to be here; a creature native to another plane is instead sent home. If your concentration holds the full minute, an extraplanar target does not come back.
The target's AC cannot be lower than 16 for the duration, regardless of armor worn.
Hurl a weapon or ammunition to conjure a barrage; each creature in a 60ft cone takes 3d8 of the weapon's damage type (DEX save half).
Declare it, and for one scene no ally within your sight dies. They fall, they bleed, they are dragged from the field — and every one of them wakes up. Your enemies enjoy no such protection.

Another's fortune is yours to nudge: steal a stumble from an ally's slip or gift one to an enemy's sure step (±1d4). A visible flicker of wrongness accompanies it — dice land on edge, bowstrings snap, the horseshoe falls.
The target blade weeps black rot: +2d6 necrotic on every hit, and a wounded foe must save (CON) or the cut festers, refusing magical healing for a day.
Up to three creatures you choose add 1d4 to their attack rolls and saving throws for the duration.
Moisture and vitality are drawn out of the target — 8d8 necrotic, CON for half. Plant creatures save at disadvantage, and ordinary plants simply die.

You know where every hidden or invisible creature within 10ft stands — breath, weight on a board, the wrongness in the air. Nothing that close can surprise you, and you strike what you cannot see there without penalty.
Teleport up to 30ft to a space you can see. On a failed DC 15 DEX check you arrive at a nearby unintended spot.
Your own spilled blood hardens into crimson plate — +2 AC, and the armor drinks the first 15 points of damage before you feel anything.
Open your own veins and the wound appears on your enemy: sacrifice any amount of your hit points, and the target loses exactly that much. No save — blood pays for blood.
Taking damage adds another 10% to the damage you cause, on top of Gathering Rage. The count resets when the fight does.
Your outline swims and doubles. Attacks against you have disadvantage unless the attacker can see without eyes or otherwise ignores illusion.

A beast of the wild has chosen you: it fights beside you (acting on your turn), shares your instincts and obeys without words. If it dies, no other will choose you for a year and a day — the wild takes bonds seriously.
Clad yourself in hardened, articulated bone platemail — the protection of plate with none of its weight or noise — for a scene.
Summon a bone dragon — wings, jaws and a breath of grave-dust — for a scene. It obeys you and nothing else.
Build a golem of bone: strong as an ogre, tireless, obedient. It lasts until destroyed; you keep one at a time.
Cast shards of bone at the target: 1d4 per caster level, out to 80 feet.
Raise structures of bone from the ground — a wall, a bridge, a cage, a stair — shaped as you will. Fails on consecrated earth.
Touch a skull or bone fragment to sense an echo of its owner's final moments — a fleeting impression, not a conversation.
The targets breathe water as easily as air for the duration. It grants no swimming speed and no protection from cold or pressure.
Roll one extra damage die whenever you land a critical hit.
Summon a storm cloud; each turn as an action, call down a bolt — creatures within 5ft of the chosen point take 3d10 lightning (DEX save half).

CAPSTONE. When all is lost, call the dawn early: every ally standing with you is healed whole, freed of fear and curse, and cannot fall below 1 HP until the fight ends. The bards will get it wrong. It was better than they say.
While you remain motionless you blend into your native surroundings (stump/foliage, stone/rockwork, or shadow by heritage) and count as hidden. Any movement ends it.
Raw negative energy ravages the body — 14d6 necrotic (CON for half), and the target's maximum hit points are reduced by the damage taken until magically restored.
A bolt strikes your chosen target for 10d8 lightning (DEX for half), then forks to as many as three more creatures within 30ft of it, each taking the same.
Every surge in your sight — yours, a miscast, an artifact's tantrum — pours power back into you instead of taking it. Standing in another caster's catastrophe, you are the only one getting stronger.
Any creature, not merely a person, regards you as a trusted friend on a failed WIS save. It will not obey obviously suicidal orders, and it knows it was charmed when the spell ends.
A vortex of life-draining negative energy surrounds you. Creatures starting their turn within 10ft take 2d8 necrotic (CON for half), and you gain half the damage dealt as hit points (up to your max).

Disease, poison, rot and afflictions of the body lift where you keep vigil: one night's work cures any single creature, and a plague ends in whatever village you stay in. It mends the body — what corrupts a soul is not your department.
Your flames read intent: allies standing in fire you made take no harm and knit closed instead, and your fire ignores resistance — the wild flame is older than any ward built against it.

Read unguarded moments — microexpressions, involuntary word choices, measured silences — with uncomfortable precision. Advantage on Insight checks to notice what someone is deliberately NOT saying, and to gauge the gap between what they say and what they mean.
Fuses two or more of your undead servants into a single greater horror — hit points and strength pooled, and the whole crueler than its parts.

Speak a one-word command (approach, drop, flee, grovel, halt, or similar); the target makes a WIS save or obeys on its next turn. It will not obey a directly harmful command, and the spell fails if it cannot understand you or is undead.
Once per day, briefly commune with a recently dead creature; for up to a minute it answers a few questions tersely and truthfully, limited to what it knew in life.
Seizes lasting control of an undead creature. Mindless undead simply obey; an intelligent one repeats its save at each dawn.

Ground you hallow is yours: nothing unholy crosses it uninvited — undead and fiends must fight their own nature to come within 10ft — and the dying inside it do not slip away. A night's rite makes the consecration hold, and anyone who sleeps within wakes as though rested a week. Raising a new place lets the old go quiet.

Every weapon your party carries counts as blessed while you are in the fight — the ghost, the fiend, the thing ordinary steel passes straight through takes the blow like anything else. Yours in particular has no bad angles.

Command a body of water: raise a flood swell, part it to expose the bed, redirect a current, or spin a whirlpool that drags in vessels and swimmers (STR to pull free). One mode at a time, changeable each round.
The surge is no longer blind. When your magic answers with its own idea it offers two, and you choose which one happens. Chaos has stopped happening to you and started negotiating.

Roll a d20 against every melee attack made on you. On a roll under your character level you counter: you take HALF damage from that attack and immediately answer with an attack of your own. The trade is deliberate — you eat part of the blow to open the attacker up. At high level a Warrior surrounded by blades is the most dangerous thing in the room.
A slow fog of decay crawls across the ground, advancing 10ft per round. Everything it passes over withers — 3d6 necrotic (CON for half); ordinary plant life dies outright.
When a foe drops to your attack, your momentum carries into the next: immediately strike another target in reach or range. The chain breaks only when you miss.
Condemns the target to the caster's equivalent of Hell.  A WIS saving throw spares the target the trip but holds them in place and causes fire damage.

No darkness is dark to you, mundane or magical, and the dark answers small requests: torches gutter, shadows pool and stretch, a corner is unlit when you need one. Something on the far side of the dark knows your name now.
Immune to all forms of decay, disease, and death or blood magic.
Magical darkness fills a 15ft-radius sphere; it blocks darkvision and ordinary light cannot illuminate it.
See in darkness within 60ft as though it were dim light, in shades of grey. Does not pierce magical darkness.
Sense undead, corpses, and death-taint within 60ft without seeing them, and gain advantage on Arcana/Lore checks about undead, curses, or death magic.
Step between the worlds of the living and dead: move up to INT x 5 ft unimpeded through creatures, objects, and difficult terrain, ignoring opportunity attacks.

CAPSTONE. In a battle you are fighting in, name the victor and the field goes that way: reinforcements arrive, the flank folds, the champion's horse throws them. The outcome is yours. The cost in the dead is not, and you will be counting it afterwards.

When you or anyone you can see drops, death is told to wait: they stand at 1 hit point instead of falling. The same creature cannot be spared twice in one day — the second time, the god is not listening.
Undead of lesser standing than you no longer flee when you turn them — they come apart where they stand. Anything older or greater than you still runs, and remembers who made it run.
A carefully drawn sigil that snares the first devil, demon, or undead to cross it — held fast within the circle (CHA negates on entry) until any line of the design is broken.
The target's skin hardens into faceted crystal, resistant to slashing and piercing for the duration. Light fractures off every plane of you — stealth is impossible while it lasts.
Sets a corpse alight with unholy flame. Any creature that touches or strikes the pyre takes 2d10 fire-and-necrotic damage, and the flame leaps hungrily at attackers.
Requires a focus object. While you focus on a target, every 5 hit points it loses are stored as 1 mana in the focus. The stored mana can later be drawn into you as a supply.
Every healing you work gives back more than it should, and your hands read a body at a touch: what broke it, how long it has, and whether the trouble is wound, poison, sickness or grief.
Illusorily change your appearance — body and clothing/gear — until the spell ends. Physical inspection or an Investigation check reveals the disguise.

A thin green ray unmakes what it touches. A creature that fails its DEX save takes 10d6+40 force; one reduced to 0 HP crumbles to fine grey dust — beyond the reach of Resurrection, which needs a body. A Wall of Force or 10ft cube of nonmagical matter is simply annihilated.

End one ongoing spell of 3rd tier or lower on the target automatically. For a higher-tier effect, make a spellcasting ability check (DC 10 + that spell's tier). Only affects ongoing magical effects, not instantaneous ones already resolved.
Pray aloud for your god to act directly. Roll d100; under your level it does — plainly, publicly, and in its own way. Answered or not, it will not be asked again for seven days.
Your god blesses your weapon: once per turn a hit carries an extra d8 of your deity's own kind — light, flame, frost, rot — and the wound is unmistakably divine to anyone who looks at the body.

Once per long rest, offer a creature a moment of genuine, non-magical safety. It gains advantage on its next Insight or Persuasion check made in your presence, and you learn one true thing it believes about itself.
You attack twice on your turn instead of once, and may split the two attacks between different targets.

Exhale destructive energy of your draconic bloodline — a 15ft cone or a 30ft line by heritage; each creature in the area takes 2d6 of your element (fire, cold, lightning, or acid), halved on a successful DEX save. Recharges on a rest.
A melee or 30ft necrotic touch; deal 1d6 necrotic and regain HP equal to half the damage dealt.
Cast druid spells while in Wild Shape — the beast's throat carries the words.
Minor nature magic: predict the next 24h weather, make a flower bloom, create a harmless sensory effect, or light/snuff a small flame.
+1 maximum HP per character level.
The ground shakes, stones rise from the earth and tip over, enemies and walls alike crash to the ground.
Knocks the target's soul clean out of its body. The vacant body stands slack and defenseless while the drifting soul can only watch; the soul snaps back when the spell ends — if the body still lives.
Tendrils of void energy race outward in a line — 2d4 negative damage and a lingering bleed; CON for half and no bleed.
Resistance (half damage) to one elemental damage type — fire, cold, lightning, or acid — fixed by your heritage.
Your Wild Shape reaches past flesh: elemental bodies — living flame, stone, water, wind — once per day each. The beasts were practice.

Your element cannot harm you, and it answers small requests without a spell: candle-flames bow, frost blooms across a window, sparks leap to your palm. Your spells of that element roll one extra damage die.
Your rage lasts as long as the fight does, and dropping to 0 HP does not end it — you get one more round of fury on your feet before your body files its complaint.
The next time you hit with a weapon this turn, thorny vines sprout; the target makes a STR save or is restrained, taking 1d6 piercing each turn until it breaks free.
Grasping weeds fill a 20ft square (difficult terrain); a creature there makes a STR save or is restrained until it breaks free with a STR check.

For one scene you are the ending of things: nonliving matter you touch turns to dust outright, hostile magic gutters out within 30ft of you, and living creatures who stand against you age a year and take 4d10 necrotic each round.
No non-magical binding holds you: rope, manacles, chains, a locked cell, a press of hands. Given a few unobserved moments you are simply out. Magical restraints still hold.
On a FAILED DEX save against an area effect, take half damage instead of full. (Class-feature Evasion later upgrades this to zero on a success.)
Double your proficiency bonus on Deception checks.
Double your proficiency bonus on Stealth checks.
Detonates a corpse in a burst of bone shards and rot — 6d6 damage to everything within 10ft, DEX for half.
Allies inside your aura stand in the eye: your weather never touches them, and arrows shot into it are slapped aside by the wind.
Your claws and fangs bite through wards meant for steel (they count as magical), and the beast's throat can still carry your casting — roar the spell.
Study a creature for a breath and it is your quarry: you read its trail, its wounds and its next move, and your first strike against it each scene lands where it hurts.

Any feat of raw athleticism an ordinary human could dream of, you can simply do: leap the chasm, kick the oak door off its hinges, climb the sheer wall in rain, carry the wounded ox home. Feats at the very edge of mortal possibility may demand a check; feats within mortal imagination do not.
Advantage on initiative. If you are surprised while raging, you act normally anyway.

Detailed operational intelligence on organizations you have worked inside: chains of command, acquisition strategies, prior operations, funding sources. Your recall of a former employer's operations is treated as reliable; specifics live on your sheet.
A 30ft radius where everything ends faster: structures sag and crack, potions spoil, food blackens, healing is halved, and objects age a year every round.

Choose one, permanently, when you gain this: Archery (+2 to ranged attacks), Defense (+1 AC in armor), Dueling (+2 damage with a lone one-handed weapon), Two-Weapon (add your modifier to the off-hand hit), Great Weapon (reroll 1s and 2s on two-handed damage), or Protection (once per round, impose disadvantage on an attack against an adjacent ally).
Summon a loyal spirit steed (warhorse, pony, etc.) bonded to you telepathically; it serves as a mount and ally until it drops to 0 HP or you dismiss it.
A ranged spell attack hurling a mote of fire; 1d8 fire on a hit. Ignites unattended flammable objects. Damage scales with caster level, not slots.
A lance of flame; 1d10 fire on a hit and ignites unattended flammable targets.
Resistance (half damage) to fire damage.
A bright streak blossoms into flame at a point you choose; each creature in a 20ft-radius sphere makes a DEX save, taking 8d6 fire (half on a success). Ignites unattended flammable objects.

Whistle up a wildfire the size of a hill and walk it like a hound: it moves where you point, spares every living thing you name, and where it has passed, flowers open by morning. Armies break before it; forests thank you after.

Step into any fire you can see and out of any other: a candle is a door, a burning village is a hall of doors. Once per scene, arrive as a burst — 2d8 fire around your exit, allies excepted, as always.

Causes a rush of water to issue forth from the caster's outstretched hands causing all entities within range to attempt a STR save or be washed back 100 feet taking tumbling damage.  Small creatures get no saving throw, giant creatures get a bonus +2 to saving throw.
Stitches several corpses into one hulking flesh golem bound to your will. It does not tire, does not fear, and does not question.
The Ranger conjures a dozen ethereal arrows.  +2 to hit, +2 to damage.
A bank of dense fog rolls out and fills the area, heavily obscuring everything inside it. Creatures within cannot see out, and those outside cannot see in. A strong wind disperses it in a round.
Your power is a reservoir in the blood, not a book. You always know exactly how much magic you have left, and at a glance how nearly spent any other caster in sight is. The reading is never wrong.

The target ignores difficult terrain; magic can neither reduce its speed nor paralyze nor restrain it; it slips any grapple, manacle or net by spending 5ft of movement; and water imposes no penalty on its movement or attacks.
The gap between you and your prey is never safe: leap your full movement onto any foe, arriving as an attack that puts them on the ground (STR resists the knockdown).
Each attack after the first in a fight adds another 10% to the damage you deal, building as long as you keep swinging. Stop, and the count starts over.

Three warrior-shaped constructs of living gemstone rise where you point (AC 17, 40 HP each). They act on your turn and obey your spoken commands; at 0 HP or when the spell ends they shatter into worthless shards.
Ordinary vermin swell to monstrous size — a spider the size of a hound, a wasp like a hawk — and obey your spoken commands. They revert when the spell ends or they are slain.
The target and everything it wears and carries vanish completely. Unlike lesser invisibility, attacking and casting do NOT break it — only the spell's end brings the target back into view.
Ends one severe affliction on the target: a curse, a petrification, a charm or possession, one level of exhaustion, or any reduction to its ability scores or maximum HP.
Once per day you bind at 30ft the instant death occurs, and your vessels hold souls indefinitely.
When you kill a creature with a spell, regain HP equal to twice the spell's tier. Once per turn.
Raises a six-foot obelisk of fused bone. Each round it stands, it drags one skeleton out of the earth to serve you — one per round, for half your level in rounds.
You link a party in silent speech — everyone hears everyone, at a mile's spread, through walls and noise. Perfect for a heist and ruinous for an argument; a linked creature may close its end at will.
Once per fight a miss becomes a hit — yours, or any companion's you can see. Your god corrects the swing visibly, and everyone on the field knows whose hand did it.
Your next ranged weapon hit bursts into thorns: creatures within 5ft of the target take 1d10 piercing (DEX save half).
A surge of pure life restores the target to perfect health.  All HP are restored.  All negative effects are removed.  Any missing limbs are restored. Undead and constructs are untouched.
Ruptures the target's vessels from within — 4d6 necrotic, and they bleed 1d4 per round until tended. CON for half and no bleed.
A magnificent feast appears. Those who share the full hour are cured of disease and poison, and for 24 hours are immune to poison and to fear, and carry 2d10 bonus maximum HP.

You disappear into whatever surrounds you. In a crowd or a household you become one of them — posture, pace and business all wrong for the person being hunted. In the wild you take on the cover itself: motionless against rock, bracken or snow, effectively invisible to a passing eye. Someone actively searching may contest with Perception; acting overtly ends it.
Paralyzes any creature — beast, fiend, giant, anything with a mind to seize, not merely humanoids. Attacks against the frozen target from within 5ft strike true and deadly.
Paralyzes undead where they stand. Mindless undead get no save; intelligent ones repeat theirs at the end of each round.

A real hole, 5ft across and 10ft deep, opens in floor or wall. A creature standing there makes a DEX save or drops in (2d6). When the spell ends the hole seals — anything still inside is shunted out, prone.

Create a zone of consecrated ground.  The zone may not be crossed by undead, devils, or demons.  Undead, devils, or demons in the zone at the time of casting are immediately repelled  to the nearest available boundary.  In the event no escape is available, Divine damage equal to the caster's level * 10 is applied per round.
Sucks the moisture from every living thing in the area — 10d8 necrotic, CON for half. Plant and water-born creatures save at disadvantage.
Whisper a name into a shadow and a hound of it steps out to harry that creature. It does not tire, it does not lose the trail, and its quarry sleeps badly until the hound is called off or destroyed.
Accurately identify and describe a plant or animal in the druid's line of sight. Includes alchemical uses as well as animal abilities and behaviors.

You give the target a memory of something that did not happen, no longer than a few minutes and no more unlikely than their own life allows. They recall it as their own and will act and testify on it. Hard evidence to the contrary lets them doubt it. The counterpart to Oubliate: this ADDS to what a mind holds rather than taking away.
Once per rest, reroll a saving throw you have just failed and take the second result. You set your feet against the thing that should have moved you.

Once per day, when a chosen target is within 150 feet, nothing bars your approach: walls have gaps, wards have seams, guards are looking elsewhere, and you arrive at the target's side as though the fortress itself conspired. Beyond 150 feet the fortress owes you nothing. The approach is movement only — the kill is still yours to make, and leaving is your own problem.
A roiling sphere of biting locusts. The area is lightly obscured, difficult terrain; a creature entering it or starting its turn there makes a CON save against 4d10 piercing.

Every Constitution saving throw you make succeeds automatically — poison, disease, exhaustion, the cold that kills lesser men — except on a natural 1, which fails as it always would. Your body has stopped negotiating.

No soul passes within a mile without your leave: the dying linger until you rule, and the dead cannot be raised against you. Once — only once — you may spend every soul you hold to call one person truly back to life.
Lies rot in your gaze: you always know when you're told a falsehood, and once per scene you may compel one creature to answer a single question truly.

While you still have hit points, nothing takes you out of the fight: you cannot be stunned, paralyzed, restrained, knocked prone, disarmed, grappled, or moved against your will, by any means mundane or magical. You can be killed. You cannot be handled — and every commander who has faced you knows it.
A mote of living wildfire rides with you: hurl it each round (1d8 fire, 30ft, no mana), and it never touches what you love — your fire cannot harm an ally unless you will it.
Any beast will hear you out. Once per scene, ask the wild a favor — a hawk to carry word, wolves to harry a column, rats to empty a granary by dawn.
A sharp clang unlocks or unbars one locked/stuck object within range. The knock is audible out to 300ft.
Brush, bog, scree and snow cost you nothing: you move through wild ground at full pace where others crawl, and thorns and briars part rather than tear.

Pain, exhaustion, and wounds do not slow you: you fight at full strength however hurt you are, and conditions that would merely slow or weaken you do not (those that bind, charm, or fell you outright still can). While an ally is in danger you do not drop from wounds alone — you go down when the fight is done, or when death itself takes you.
After one pass through a building or location, retain an accurate mental map of it: entry points, weak latches, guard rhythms, storage placement.
The target's jumping distance triples — rooftop to rooftop, a chasm, a courtyard wall. It does not slow a fall at the far end.
A foe you drop from stealth goes down silently — no cry, no clatter, no alarm — and nothing you do in darkness reveals where you are.

Recall with perfect clarity any contract, debt, name, or obligation you have personally witnessed or been bound to. An INT check (DC 12) identifies whether a symbol, cipher, or document belongs to a known contractual tradition.
Your companion has grown into something from the old stories — dire-sized, cunning as a person, known by name in three kingdoms. Enemies plan around it now, not you.

If an object is within your reach, you can already have taken it — pockets picked, rings slipped from fingers, a knife from its sheath — with none the wiser at the time. Victims discover the loss later. A creature actively watching its property may contest with Perception against your Sleight of Hand.
End one disease OR one condition on a creature: blinded, deafened, paralyzed, or poisoned.
WIS save or the target loses up to 15 minutes of memory per point of your INT modifier — recent events simply vanish. The narrative-only sibling of Oubliate.
An object you touch sheds bright light in a 20ft radius and dim light 20ft beyond — steady, heatless, and smotherable by covering the object. Casting it again moves the glow.
Your radiance becomes a fact of the region: within your aura all healing is doubled, all darkness is merely shade, and lies stumble on their way out of the mouth.
Your next ranged attack becomes lightning: 4d8 lightning on a hit (2d8 on a miss), and creatures within 10ft of the target take 2d8 (DEX save half).
Point at what the sky should hate: once per round a bolt falls on a foe within 60ft.
Name or picture a creature you have seen; you sense the direction and rough distance to the nearest instance of it within 1000ft. Running water wider than 10ft breaks the trail.
Open locks and disarm mechanical traps with a DEX check against the device's DC. Requires thieves' tools.
Conjure a floating spectral hand that can manipulate objects, open unlocked doors/containers, and carry up to 10 lb. It cannot attack, activate magic items, or wield weapons.
Three darts of force strike targets you can see, one dart each or combined; each auto-hits for 1d4+1 force. No attack roll, no save.
The flesh is half power now. You barely need food, sleep or air; poison and disease find nothing to grip; you age at a crawl. The frailty remains — what cuts you still cuts.

Ignite up to 6 mana in the target's pool, destroying it; the combusting mana sears them for 1 damage per point destroyed. A WIS save halves both the mana destroyed and the damage (rounded down). A creature without a mana pool is unaffected.
Tear up to 4 mana from the target's pool; half of what is torn free (rounded down) flows into your own pool. A creature without a mana pool is unaffected.
A whole room takes you for a friend on a failed WIS save — a guardroom, a council, a crowd. Each knows it was charmed afterwards, which makes this a spell that buys time and costs reputation.

Given moments and whatever is at hand — kitchen herbs, lamp oil, the scorpion from a boot — you render any food, drink, or weapon lethally poisoned, instantly and creatively. Onset and symptoms are yours to design: immediate, slow, or mimicking illness. Ordinary folk simply succumb; hardened or named foes may resist with a CON save.

Bend a spell's shape as you cast it: quicken it to an instant, twin it onto a second target, stretch its range or duration, or work it with no word or gesture at all. One shaping per casting, on top of the spell's own cost.
A cloud of despair; creatures inside are wracked with grief and hopelessness — WIS save or act at disadvantage while within it.
Create either a sound or a static visual image no larger than a 5ft cube; an Investigation check discerns it is false.

Spend your god's authority out loud and it answers in its own idiom — light in a dark place, a binding broken, a frightened crowd's courage handed back. The god answers the priest, not the request: what arrives is what your deity would give, not what you asked for.
Three illusory duplicates flit around you; when something targets you, an attack may strike a duplicate instead (destroying it) rather than you.
Strength and Constitution push past the mortal ceiling. Doors, chains and 'impossible' are all suggestions now.
Resistance to necrotic damage and advantage on death saving throws. Undead you control cannot be turned by clerics or paladins.
Resistance (half damage) to necrotic damage.

The first time in a scene you would be seized, cornered, bound, or otherwise physically taken, you simply are not — you were already elsewhere, and those present half-remember deciding to let you go. Does not prevent damage, only capture.
You see perfectly in any darkness, mundane or magical, and darkness likes you back: within 30ft of you torches gutter and lanterns shrink to a glow.

Locks, knots, seals, shackles, and mechanical traps open for you as though they wanted to: given a few moments and anything resembling a pick, treat them as unlocked. Masterwork or magical closures take longer and may demand a check, but never stop you cold — a lock is a suggestion.
Your named enemy cannot lose you: you sense their direction within a day's ride, and while the hunt is on you need half the sleep and none of the comfort.
Your weapon carries your oath without being asked: every hit deals +1d8 radiant, and creatures of darkness find the light sticky — it clings, and marks them for everyone to see.

The dragon in your line wakes. Fine scales harden your skin where armor would sit (+1 AC unarmored); one element runs in your veins, chosen once — flame, frost, storm or venom; and dragons and their kin know you on sight for what you carry.

Surrounded is where you are strongest: when several foes engage you in melee, every one of them is within your reach, none of them gains any edge from numbers, and a blow that fells one may carry into the next. A room of soldiers is a queue.
Starlight thins you: blades and arrows dim as they land, you no longer need sleep or breath — you keep watch the way the stars do — and moonlight and starlight bear your weight as solid ground.
In natural terrain you cannot be tracked, ambushed or outpaced, and beasts will not raise a claw against you unprovoked.
Once per short rest, assess a person's likely loyalty, fear threshold, or hidden motive with a WIS check (DC 12). On a success, the GM reveals one concealed motivation.
WIS save or surgically erase ONE specific person or event from the target's memory entirely (the engine scrubs it via [NPC_FORGET:]); they cannot recall it even when reminded.

Push a spell past its ceiling: maximum possible effect, no roll. The price is paid in your own body — 1d6 per tier of the spell — and those wounds refuse all healing until you next sleep. The power was never free; it was borrowed.
You fight as one animal in two bodies: when either of you lands a hit, the other may immediately strike the same target.
Your presence is an oath others lean on: allies who can see you cannot be charmed or made afraid — and your word, once given, is impossible for you to break, and everyone can feel that it is.
You and allies within 30ft gain +10 to Stealth and cannot be tracked by nonmagical means, leaving no tracks or scent.
The path to becoming a lich is open to you. It is taken once and cannot be untaken.
Causes the target to suffer damage equivalent to all damage they've caused during the current conflict.

Craft an illusion in ONE target's mind that it believes is real — it rationalizes any illogic away. Only the target perceives it. If the phantasm would harm it (fire, a collapsing beam), it takes 1d6 psychic each round it is affected. An action + INT check lets it disbelieve.
Overgrow a 100ft radius into difficult terrain (movement quartered) — or, over 8 hours, enrich the land for a year of bountiful harvest.
Natural poisons and venoms have no effect on you.

Transforms the target into a beast of your choice of equal or lesser power — its gear melds away, its mind dulls to the beast's, and it uses the beast's body as temporary vitality. It reverts when that vitality is spent or the spell ends, at the HP it had before.
Project your mind into one of your undead thralls, seeing and speaking through it; your own body lies in suspended animation until you withdraw.
On a declared attack, add +1d6 damage on a hit. Declared before the roll.

Let the old blood fill the room. Lesser creatures' nerve breaks under your attention — they flee, freeze or yield (WIS resists); hardened ones bargain more carefully. Neither charm nor fear: the older thing both descend from.
Catch someone in the first moments after death — a creature dead less than a minute stands again at 1 hit point, whole enough to walk. What they saw while they were gone is between them and your god.
Minor magical tricks: light or snuff a small flame, clean or soil an object, chill/warm/flavor food, make a harmless sensory effect, or a trivial mark.
Your charge breaks formations: shield walls scatter, gates crack, cavalry balks. Enemy commanders write their orders around where you might be.

The totem wears YOU: become the spirit made flesh for a scene — a bear the size of a wagon, an eagle that blots the torchlight, a wolf out of the first winter. Your legend and the spirit's are the same story now.
A flame in your hand sheds light; you may hurl it as a ranged spell attack for 1d8 fire (ending the spell).
The target grows short but sharp quills which will damage any opponent touching them.
Enter a battle fury: +2 STR, +2 melee damage, and you push through pain (resist physical damage, ignore first wounds). Lasts 3 rounds. Ends early if you take no hostile action.

Animate a fresh corpse within 10ft as a zombie thrall that follows basic commands. Requires a body present. ONE thrall at a time (until the archetype expands it); the thrall collapses if you fall unconscious.
One look tells you any creature's strengths, its weaknesses and how much fight it has left — exact wounds, what it resists, and the move it will make next.
The sky briefs you: once per scene, ask the stars one question about what is coming and receive a true sign. Any ally you share the sign with carries its light on the one roll it warned them about.
Any creature that dies within 60ft offers you its soul — no action, no vessel prepared, you ARE the vessel. Battles fill your satchel; armies feed you.
Numbers stop meaning anything: foes gain no advantage from surrounding or flanking you, their opportunity strikes miss, and when three or more engage you, it is you who has the advantage.
Once per day, when you would be reduced to 0 HP but not killed outright, you drop to 1 HP instead.

Your body closes its own wounds: you recover 1 hit point per character level for every hour that passes, resting or not. A Warrior who walks away from a battlefield is whole again by nightfall without a healer.

A night of prayer over the wounded regrows what was lost: an arm, a leg, an eye, a hand — anything short of a head. The new flesh is whole, strong and unmistakably a gift; it carries no scar, and everyone who knew the old wound knows exactly who to thank.
Return a creature that died within the last minute to life with 1 HP. Cannot restore missing body parts, revive undead/constructs, or one dead of old age.

CAPSTONE. Name one moment of pure chance — a fall, a storm, a draw, a die — and declare its outcome, however impossible. It happens exactly as spoken. Chance owed you one, and everyone watching learns it paid.
The storm carries its own: leap gaps no mortal could, and fall from any height into a thunderclap landing that costs you nothing.
CON save or the target seizes rigid and incapacitated.

Conduct binding and consecration rituals in a commanding pre-common ritual tongue: consecrate altar stones, levitate and activate attuned ritual objects, produce controlled light phenomena. Slow, deliberate workings — not combat magic.
The green fights for you unasked: difficult terrain never slows you, and once per scene the undergrowth itself restrains everything you name within 30ft.
Tree, stone and stream confide in you — what passed, when, and bleeding or not. Once per day the land opens a path: brush parts, fords surface, cliffs offer stairs.
A minute of ritual collapses years into moments on one structure: a fortress gate becomes a breach, a bridge becomes a memory, a siege engine becomes mulch. Consecrated ground resists.
Your decay no longer needs touch — corrode objects at 30ft. Once per round, when a nonmagical weapon or projectile strikes you, it decays mid-blow: damage halved, the weapon ruined.
Your body is consecrated ground: hostile magic must overcome your conviction (CHA) to touch you at all, and wherever you sleep counts as hallowed.
Poison, rot and wither slide off you and those at your side, and your body keeps the forest's calendar — you age a year for its ten.

After a day-long ritual, the target wakes: human-like intelligence, speech, and — for a plant — the power to move. It is charmed toward you for 30 days; what it chooses after that depends entirely on how you treated it.
Three rays of fire; make a separate ranged spell attack for each, 2d6 fire per hit. Split among one or more targets.
Your rage bends the weather for miles — fog to hide a retreat, a squall to ground the enemy's archers, a killing frost at midsummer. The land keeps your grudges.
The wild rises where you fight: for a scene the terrain takes your side — thorn hedges, sudden bogs, groves that hide your friends and swallow your enemies.
Wild Shape is a breath, not a ritual: shift as part of any action, gear melding or staying as you choose, and your beast ceiling keeps climbing with your level.
Your darkvision pierces even magically created darkness.
You perceive invisible creatures and objects as faint, wavering outlines.
Your smites against the named enemy cannot be resisted, reduced or forgiven — and each one breaks a hold their power has over someone else.

A dim, blade-bearing sentinel of light appears and keeps watch. Enemies that enter the watched radius or start their turn there take 20 radiant (DEX for half). The guardian fades after it has dealt 60 total damage.

When you kill, you choose what the death appears to be: a fall, a fever, a stopped heart, too much drink. Examination by ordinary means confirms your version; only magical inquiry or a master healer's close autopsy may contest it (Investigation against your Deception). What actually happened is never altered — only what the world reads from the body.

Take the form of any person or creature of roughly your size that you have seen — voice, face, bearing. It holds until you choose to end it, and does not drop when you are struck. It grants none of the form's abilities or statistics; someone who knows the original well may contest with Insight on close interaction.
Skeletal arms erupt from earth or wall to pin the target prone or against a surface; it is restrained until it snaps the bones with a STR check.

Every shadow is a door. Step into one and out of any other you have stood in before, however far — the cold between them crossed in a single held breath. What lives in that cold has learned to let you pass.

The caster takes on the physical form of anything they've touched in the past, from a chair to a dragon.  Everything is fair game.  The caster retains their intellect but any abilities associated with their previous form are swapped with the new form.
Close your eyes and use your companion's: see, hear and scent through it at any distance you could walk in a day.
A shimmering field grants a creature you can see +2 AC for the duration.
Once per round, take a blow meant for anyone within reach — and take it better than they would have: half damage to you.
Your wooden club or quarterstaff becomes magical: use your spellcasting mod for its attacks and it deals 1d8 for the duration.
The target halves in every dimension — through a grate, into a pocket, under a door. A shrunken creature has disadvantage on STR checks and deals a die less damage; an object's weight drops with it.
While raging, halve all damage that isn't an attack on your mind. Pain is information, and you've stopped reading your mail.

Decipher old and otherworldly script with scholarly fluency — ritual markings, ward anchors, contract notation. Passive identification on contact with inscribed stone or bound material; reading tells you what it SAYS, not whether it is safe.
Create a purely visual illusion no larger than a 15ft cube; you can move it. Physical interaction or an Investigation check reveals it is false.
You move without sound. Floorboards, gravel, dry leaves and armour make no noise for you; a creature cannot detect you by hearing alone, and Stealth checks ignore penalties for noisy footing.
Drains 3d6 hit points from the target directly into you — what it loses, you gain.
The creatures out of old stories are just bigger quarry: your weapons wound anything however warded, and no aura of terror, majesty or size makes your hands hesitate.

Roll 5d8: that many hit points of creatures fall unconscious, starting with the least wounded and working up until the pool runs out. Undead and creatures immune to charm are unaffected; damage or a hard shake wakes a sleeper.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Internal contradiction: The effect starts with the least wounded, while the targets field says weakest first and the HP-pool rule depends on remaining hit points. Specify the intended order; do not silently swap these meanings.

reviews.replacement: Feign death on yourself or a creature you touch — indistinguishable from a true corpse (no breath, no pulse). A self-cast always lasts the full duration.
You are Small: advantage on Stealth to hide behind larger creatures and you can move through a larger creature's space, but you have disadvantage attacking with Heavy weapons.
Double the attack's damage dice when you have advantage, are unseen, or the target is flanked by an ally. Once per turn.
Ten quiet minutes give back what a night gives other casters: recover half your mana. Once per day — a sorcerer who catches their wind is a sorcerer rearmed.
Imprisons the target's soul inside a prepared gem; the body collapses comatose. Shattering the gem frees the soul. Fails against creatures more powerful than the caster.
Pour a bound soul into a fresh corpse: the dead walks again with its own memories and skills intact — a thinking servant, not a shambler. It knows exactly what it owes you.

Your blade drinks the soul of what it cuts: choose one ability the victim possesses and it becomes yours for the next 4 hours, and theirs no longer while you hold it. You may hold three such abilities at once; while all three are held the blade takes nothing new until one expires or you release it. Releasing is a moment's will, and returns the ability to its owner if they live.
A bound soul is fuel: consume one to regain mana equal to the soul's level, or to cast your next spell as if one tier higher. The soul is spent forever — it does not pass on, it burns.

CAPSTONE. From one dusk to the next dawn the night is yours: every shadow a door, every darkness your eyes and ears, every dark thing yours to command. One night to move an army unseen, empty a fortress, or visit every enemy you have at once. Then the sun rises, and the debt is even.
Ask a corpse (with a mouth, dead no more than 10 days, not undead) up to five questions; it answers briefly and cryptically from what it knew in life.
Binds an undead target to a place or object against its will; it cannot stray more than 60ft from its anchor, and its rage tends to show.

Casting and striking are one motion: a spell you cast travels through the steel and lands with the blow, so the cut and the magic arrive together. The spell's own cost is still paid and its save still applies; what you gain is that no enemy gets the moment between the incantation and the stroke.
The target climbs sheer walls and ceilings with hands free, moving at its normal pace across any solid surface.
The ground in a 20ft radius sprouts spikes (difficult terrain); a creature takes 2d4 piercing for every 5ft it travels through the area.
Spectral guardians swirl in a 15ft aura; hostile creatures there move at half speed and take 3d8 (WIS save half) when they enter or start their turn there.
Sleep, and send your spirit out in the totem's shape for an hour — scout the pass, circle the camp, whisper to your kin in their dreams. Your body lies defenseless meanwhile.
Create a floating spectral weapon; a bonus action moves it 20ft and makes a melee spell attack for 1d8 + your spellcasting modifier force.
Your mind holds two workings at once: sustain two concentration spells simultaneously. Losing one does not shake the other.
Stars fall from the heavens pummeling the earth when they land.
While underground or touching stone you always know your approximate depth and direction; advantage on checks about the origin or construction of stonework.

Your rage wears weather — choose it: lightning (attackers take 1d8 back), thunder (your blows throw foes off their feet), or frost (everything near you slows). The sky above you agrees with your mood.

Your feats of strength exceed the mortal: hold the falling gate on your shoulders, bend the portcullis, throw a spear the length of a field, drag the beached warship to the water. Bards argue over which of the stories about you are true; all of them are. Feats that would rival giants may demand a check — the GM narrates the rest as fact.

When you hit, you may forgo the damage entirely and strike to stun instead — the pommel to the temple, the flat of the blade behind the ear. The target makes a CON save; on a failure it is stunned for one round and its guard is wide open. Any given creature can be caught by this only ONCE: a foe who has felt it never falls for the same blow twice.
Fills the target with an overwhelming sense of calm and security.

You plant a suggestion no more unreasonable than something the target might plausibly have thought; on a failed WIS save they remember it as their OWN idea and will argue for it to others as such. Ordering them into obvious harm breaks it immediately.
Summon fey spirits in beast form (their total power scaling with the slot) that obey your commands and fight for you until the spell ends.

Summon Item — Teleports a small item to the hand of the rogue. Works on any item within 30 feet if the rogue knows its location. Does NOT require line of sight.  The Rogue must be aware of the item they're summoning, ex: "I summon the ring from the safe" works, but "I summon whatever is in the safe" does not.

A beam of brilliant sunlight blazes from your hand in a 60ft line — 10d8 radiant, CON for half, the failed save also blinding until your next turn. You can sweep it to a new line each round. It is true sunlight, with everything that means for creatures that fear it.

Your blade cuts magic as though it were rope: sever a standing enchantment, cut a summoned creature from the anchor that holds it here, part a wall of flame or force to walk through. Effects sustained by a living caster within reach may resist with a contest of their will against your strike; unattended magic simply parts.
Disadvantage on attack rolls and on sight-based Perception checks while you, or the thing you are looking at, is in direct sunlight.
See in darkness within 120ft as though it were dim light, in shades of grey — the extended sight of the deep-dwelling races.

Once per combat, declare the impossible shot — a ricochet off a helm, a bank off the temple bell, a needle threaded through an arrow slit at extreme distance. The attack hits and is a critical hit no matter how absurd the path; if any part of the target can be seen, it can be killed. The GM narrates the path the shot takes.
Once per rest, take one additional action on your turn — a second attack sequence, a dash, a shove, a shout that rallies the line. The surge is a burst of trained speed, not magic.
Your quiver refills itself faster than you can empty it. While the spell lasts you loose two extra ranged attacks each round, the ammunition dissolving to mist after it lands.

You make yourself the only thing in the fight worth killing — a bellow, an insult, a raised visor. For 3 rounds every foe who heard you attacks YOU if able, leaving your companions unmarked. Ordinary foes simply comply; named or formidable ones may resist with a WIS save.

Move a creature or heavy object up to 30ft each round by thought alone — an unwilling creature contests your spellcasting with its STR each round it is held. Fine work at a distance is yours too: thrown levers, turned keys, knots untied.

You open a private two-way channel of thought with one creature you can see. Words and images pass instantly and silently; the other party knows exactly who is speaking and may simply refuse to answer.
Your frenzy is a weapon everyone else feels: foes who watch you drop one of their own must check their nerve (WIS) or give ground.
Foes you strike from darkness or ambush must check their nerve (WIS) or panic — a camp you hit at night starts breaking before it forms ranks.
A minor divine display: boom your voice, flicker flames, cause tremors, sound a phantom noise, or fling open unlocked doors/windows.

You see the whole engagement at once: where reinforcements will enter, when morale will break, which flank is soft, what each combatant is about to attempt. The GM tells you the true state of any fight you can see, and you are never surprised by a development a soldier could have foreseen.
Your body answers the wild directly: your unarmed strikes and grapples land like a great beast's (a foe you grapple cannot break free without magic), and on all fours you outrun horses.

Once, when death takes you, the bond refuses it: you wake whole where your bonded weapon lies, hilt already in your hand, however far that is from where you fell. What happened to you still happened — the wound, the fall, the grief of those who watched — you simply are not dead of it.
Your boons outlast the danger that prompted them. Any blessing you lay on a companion runs until your next rest instead of fading with the fight — a party that travels with you travels blessed.

Your strikes find the places that matter — joints, arteries, the gap in the plate. Wounds you deal are graver than they have any right to be: foes bleed, limp, and favor a side, and they remember who gave them the scar. The GM narrates your solid hits as telling ones.

One look at a place and you know it: where the valuables are, where the strongbox hides, who carries the keys, and every way out — including the ones the owner has forgotten. The GM answers honestly; things concealed by magic may stay hidden.

Once, call out any creature by name. It must meet you alone in single combat, and the world clears a circle: while the duel holds, no creature, spell, or power outside it may touch what happens within, and neither of you may leave until one yields or falls. The fight itself is still yours to win — the circle only makes it fair.

Pull others through with you: carry companions along a Shadow Walk, or drag an enemy into the cold between (CHA resists) and finish the conversation there, in a realm where every advantage is yours. Its native things treat you as one of their lords.

Call a piece of the sky down: 4d10 radiant in a 10ft ring and every foe inside knocked from their feet. The crater glows until dawn, and nothing inside its light can hide from you — not behind stone, spell or skin.
CAPSTONE. Declare the Accounting against your named enemy: neither of you can die, flee or be aided until one yields or falls. Every debt settles inside that circle.

Wear the First Beast — the shape all animals remember in their bones. For a scene, everything wild within a mile answers its cry as kin, and nothing mortal that sees it ever quite settles on what it was.

reviews.key: the first blow is the last
reviews.replacement: Your first strike against a creature that does not suspect the attack is an automatic critical hit. Against ordinary folk the fight is usually over before it begins; against hardened or named foes it opens with the worst wound they will take.

CAPSTONE. Set the First Fire in the wound: the dead thing burns for a single heartbeat and stands back up new-grown and whole. The fire keeps your warmth as its tithe — ever after, flames bow away from you, and you will never be warm again.
Your healing pool doubles, and Lay on Hands now mends minds as well as bodies — madness, despair and magical corruption end at your touch.

Call your deity onto the field, and it comes visibly — a wave of standing light, a shadow in armor twelve feet tall — and fights beside you for that encounter, as capable as you are. Everyone present sees it. Word of it travels ahead of you.
Every beast of your totems' kind within the valley answers your call, and the spirits of the wild deal with you as an equal, not a guest.

Ground your fire has touched is yours for a season: it regrows overnight — greener, taller, wilder — and while you stand on land you have burned and reborn, your casts cost one less mana and fire cannot harm you at all.
You swore to the life older than the gods: wild places accept you as kin, your smites bloom with thorned light, and once per scene the vines answer you — grasping, tripping, holding fast.
Take the middle shape: your hands and voice with the beast's strength and senses — cast, speak, climb and rend in the same body.
Once per scene, make the shot no one else would attempt — through the arrow slit, the rope at fifty paces, the apple off the moving cart. Declare it; it lands.

Once, steal a thing no hand should hold: a god's flame, the luck of a house, a word from a language, the color from a king's banner. The theft is real — you hold it and the owner lacks it — and the world adjusts around the fact. It creates a possession, never unwrites the past; how the stolen thing behaves in your keeping is the GM's to narrate.

Once, name a target. From that moment their death is a matter of when, not if: the story bends toward the ending you have chosen — doors sit unlocked, guard shifts change early, the poison is on the right shelf, the storm grounds their ship. The world supplies opportunity, never the kill itself; you must still take it, and the target may yet make their ending costly.

The weight of your god hangs on your voice. Small commands spoken directly — kneel, drop it, wait, speak — land unless the target has real cause to resist, and even then defiance is visible effort. You never puppet a body; you press a will, and its owner is awake for every moment of it.

CAPSTONE. Name a single creature the object of your Last Great Hunt: no distance, disguise or plane hides it from your pursuit, and when you finally close, your killing shot cannot be prevented — only survived.

CAPSTONE. Declare the Last Red Day: until the battle ends you cannot die, cannot tire, and cannot be stopped by anything smaller than the battle itself. When it ends you sleep for a week — win or lose.

CAPSTONE. Speak one decree over a place and it becomes law in the oldest sense: the land itself enforces it. No blood spilled in this valley. No lie spoken in this city. It holds until a god's own authority overturns it, and your name is on it forever.
Your Hunter's Mark never fades until you release it. You know the direction and freshness of your quarry's trail anywhere in the region, and it cannot lose you by mundane means.
CAPSTONE. You are the thing veterans warn recruits about. Declare a night yours: until dawn, within a mile, the darkness answers to you — who sleeps, who wakes, who is found, and who never is.

Your compulsion no longer needs your presence. A command under your seal, or carried by a messenger in your name, binds as though you spoke it eye to eye — distance was the defense, and there is no defense.

The constellations answer mid-fight: wear two at once and swap either each round. The sky over your battles is always the sky YOU need — dark for your rogues, bright for your archers, starless and silent for your escape.
Speak a wrongdoer's name before witnesses: against them you have advantage on everything — striking, tracking, resisting their arts — until justice is done. Choose carefully; the oath remembers.

A promise spoken to you binds. The oath-breaker knows the instant they break it, and so do you, wherever you are — and misfortune of your god's choosing dogs them until amends are made. Only words offered willingly can bind; a forced vow is just noise.

CAPSTONE. Kindle the Old Light — the sun the first forests grew under: within a mile, corruption burns out of land and folk alike, the wild's dead rise as allies for one battle, and what you plant that day cannot be killed by anything younger than the world.

Your invisible Mage Hand exchanges two objects of a size it can carry, and both holders go on believing they hold what they held. A creature actively watching the objects may contest with Perception against your Sleight of Hand.
