Once, lay out a plan aloud, step by step. For as long as the party follows it, it works: each step succeeds as described — the guards are where you said, the timing lands, the door is unbarred. The plan runs until the objective is achieved, a step is abandoned, or someone betrays it. The world may complicate the aftermath, never the steps themselves.

CAPSTONE. Speak the true name in your blood and your ancestor answers: the progenitor dragon itself comes, in the flesh, disposed to treat you as kin. What it does when it arrives is its own will — dragons are not tame. But it came for you, and the world saw it come.

One look at a fighter — a guard's stance, a duelist's first pass — and you know their style, their training, roughly how dangerous they are, and the mistake they are likely to make. The GM answers honestly; creatures beyond mortal warcraft may remain opaque.
CAPSTONE. Ask for one person back and be answered. Whatever remains of them — a body, a scrap, a name — they return whole and themselves, however they died and however long ago.

Your shadow can leave you: a second self of dark that walks, watches and whispers back what it sees. While it is out you cast a shadow that is not yours, and the observant notice. If it is destroyed you feel it, and it returns only at nightfall.

You can steal what is being worn, held, or watched — a sword from a hand, a ring mid-handshake, the medallion from a neck at conversation distance. An aware creature contests with Perception against your Sleight of Hand; when you win, the loss goes unnoticed until it matters.

Bring the sky down to arm's reach for a scene: your party walks on air that holds, falls simply refuse to happen, every foe stands lit by prosecutor starlight (no hiding, no feints, no borrowed faces), and one star keeps an old promise — the first ally who would die that scene, instead, does not.

You ward a place by walking its bounds with the blade drawn. While you keep the ward, no magic enters it unbidden — spells cast from outside fail at the line, and things that travel by magic arrive somewhere else — and you know the moment any arcane trespass is attempted, and from where. The ward ends when you leave the place or set it down.

You set a rumour loose about yourself or another; by the time it reaches its destination it has become true in the small ways a story needs to be — the debt was paid, the guard was bribed, the heir was seen in the city. It creates circumstance, never undoes what has already happened, and never directly harms a creature.

Once per combat, call the moment that turns the fight: trip the champion, disarm the captain, feint the line open, rally the wavering. Against ordinary foes the maneuver succeeds exactly as narrated; named or formidable foes contest it with their own warcraft.
While you stand, allies within your aura cannot be moved, felled or made to flee against their will. Lines break where you aren't.
Once per round, step from one shadow into another you can see. The dark is a hallway only you have the key to.

Stop pretending to be a person: become the storm outright for a scene — a moving column of wind, frost and lightning that armies cannot hold and arrows cannot find. Chain Lightning and Thunderwave cast themselves each round, and every blow carries Booming Blade at triple strength.

Speak one short command in your god's own voice, and every creature that hears it obeys for one action. Nothing immediately self-destructive can be commanded, and named foes get a WIS save; the rest simply do it, and remember afterwards that they did.

Bind a defeated or helpless creature into your service: awake, aware, resentful and obedient. You give orders and it carries them out hating every step — you see nothing through its eyes and speak nothing through its mouth; it serves, it is not worn. Release it, or die, and it is free.

On first contact with an unknown individual, compile a rapid threat-and-asset assessment — physical tells, visible capabilities, social patterns — and update it continuously thereafter. Observation and inference, not mind reading.
Raises up to three corpses as ghouls that obey your spoken commands; at greater power the dead rise as wights or worse.  Up to three undead may be controlled simultaneously through this spell.
A wave of force: 2d8 thunder (CON save half); creatures that fail are also pushed 10ft away. Audible out to 300ft.
Shift without count or cost, flowing form to form mid-motion — bird to bear mid-pounce. Your enemies fight a different animal every round and never the one they planned for.

Chaos likes you. When you gamble — a reckless casting, a mad plan, a coin-flip moment — fortune leans your way (advantage). In exchange your magic sometimes answers with an idea of its own: a surge the GM narrates, wondrous or inconvenient, never nothing.
Your first strike each round against a wounded or oversized foe deals +2d6 — the larger the target, the surer your point finds the seam.
The spirit stays after the rage: Bear hauls like an ox team, Eagle reads a hillside a mile off, Wolf tracks by scent alone at a dead run.

A spirit walks in your skin — choose it: Bear (halve all damage while raging), Eagle (no one you charge escapes, no one you flee catches), or Wolf (every ally fighting beside you strikes harder). The totem can be renegotiated only at a sacred site.
Leave no trail in natural terrain; cannot be tracked by nonmagical means while moving through wilderness at a careful pace.
Meditate 4 hours (semi-aware) to gain the full benefit of an 8-hour long rest; you do not sleep.
Transfers wounds from one target onto another: heal the first by up to 4d8, and an unwilling second target takes exactly what was healed (CON negates).

Once, at a moment of your choosing: you and another creature exchange places entirely — position, bonds and restraints, conditions, and the blame the situation carries. The tyrant stands in the cell wearing your charges; you stand where they stood. From that moment everyone present proceeds as though it had always been so, and acts on it.

Death cannot part you: when either of you falls, the other may share its own life to pull them back (split your remaining HP between you). And once — only once — one of you may take the other's death entirely, whatever its cause.
A second spirit accepts you: carry both totems' gifts at once. Shamans argue about whether that's allowed. The spirits don't.
You sense the presence of undead and fiends within 30ft before you see them — roughly where and that they are there, not precisely what.
Your Raise Thrall servant persists permanently until destroyed, gains bonus HP equal to your INT modifier, and can follow simple multi-step orders — go to X and perform task Y.
The first time each day you would fall, you don't: life floods back at half strength, and green shoots rise in your footprints. The old life does not let go of its sworn.
Frenzy no longer ends while enemies stand and costs no exhaustion after — and the first time each day you'd drop mid-frenzy, you stand back up at 1 HP with a 100% damage bonus until the fight ends.

As a bonus action, attune briefly to the nearest disrupted or unanchored obligation within 60ft. You do not learn its contents — only its weight (trivial, significant, or catastrophic) and roughly how long it has been loose.
Decay reaches the immaterial: end one active spell or enchantment you can see, or silence a magic item until dawn — its virtue rusts like everything else.

Probability frays around you. Locks slip, arrows curve, the one loose stone finds an enemy's foot; within 30ft the improbable becomes merely uncommon, and it is never on the other side. A GM who plans around you plans in ranges.
Your uncanny aspect unnerves others: advantage on Intimidation checks.
Blood and vitality stream out of every creature in the cone — 12d6 necrotic (CON for half), and you heal half of the total drained.
The promise of death's defeat is intoxicating: the target saves or becomes your thrall — willing, adoring, obedient. A new saving throw may be rolled every dawn.
Summons a spectral courtesan who embraces your foes — 2d6 necrotic per strike, healing you for the same amount.
A melee spell attack; 3d6 necrotic and you regain HP equal to half the damage dealt. You can attack again each turn while you concentrate.
Poison vines grow from the floor ensnaring opponents in the target area.  Saving throw vs. poison or suffer poison  damage.

Your voice issues from somewhere else — a doorway, a rafter, a statue, another person's mouth. Anything you could say, you can say from there. A suspicious listener may make an INT check to place the trick.
Step through death's door and out again: vanish and reappear beside any corpse you can sense within range. The fresher the corpse, the surer the arrival.
The land within a mile confides in you: ask it what walks, what sickens, what hides. Its answer is always true and always partial — the land has its own sense of humor.
With one action, make a ranged attack against up to 2 targets within your weapon's range.

A whirling wall of razor-edged spectral blades. Creatures passing through it, or starting their turn inside it, make a DEX save against 6d10 slashing; the wall grants three-quarters cover to those behind it.

A sheet of roaring flame springs up on a line or ring you choose; creatures in its space when it appears save DEX against 5d8 fire. One side you pick is the hot side: creatures ending their turn within 10ft of it, or passing through the wall, take 5d8 fire outright.

An invisible, utterly impassable barrier. It takes no damage from anything, blocks all physical and magical passage, and cannot be dispelled by ordinary means — only disintegration or planar travel gets past it.

A wall that shows each viewer something plausible and wrong — open road where there is a cliff, blank stone where there is a door. Creatures may pass through it freely; one who studies it and succeeds on an INT check sees it for what it is, and can then tell others.

Solid, nonmagical stone rises from the earth in shapes you choose — a wall, a bridge, a ramp, an enclosure (DEX to slip out before it closes). Held for the full duration, it becomes permanent, ordinary stone.
A rampart of tangled, finger-thick briars. Creatures in its space when it grows save DEX against 7d8 piercing; forcing a way through costs quarter speed and the same 7d8 again. It blocks sight.
reviews.notes: Second pass 2026-10-06 — Duplicate name: A separate two-space wall of  thorns entry has different damage, saves and duration. Decide whether these are two distinct abilities or which definition is authoritative before merging or renaming.

reviews.replacement: Prayer and blow are one motion. You never have to choose between casting and fighting on a turn, and armor, shield and weapon never hinder your magic — a spell of yours has been swung as often as spoken.
Your Wild Shape is built for the front line: combat forms beyond your years, shifting instant, and the beast's hide takes the first wounds meant for you.

Trained in the structural logic of protective wards: identify trigger conditions, recognition mechanisms, and whether a ward targets by intent versus by bloodline or status. Cannot always disable what it identifies — but always knows enough to warn.

Spend 10 minutes inscribing a temporary ward on a surface or object. For 24 hours, a creature attempting to alter, forge, or destroy it must succeed on a WIS save or be compelled to stop and reconsider. It delays and deters — it does not prevent a determined actor permanently.
A swarm of spectral scarabs erupts in a 30ft cone; each creature takes 3d6 necrotic (DEX save half).

You bond one weapon to yourself in an hour's ritual. It returns to your hand when called — thrown, dropped, disarmed, confiscated, buried, or an ocean away — and it cannot be taken from you while you live. You may hold one bond at a time; bonding another releases the first.
No penalty for using improvised or unfamiliar weapons — proficient with anything wieldable.

Star-charts live under your skin: each night choose a constellation to wear — the Archer (bolts of starlight, 1d8 radiant, 60ft, no mana), the Chalice (your healing spells splash 1d6 to a second ally within reach), or the Serpent (you shed dim starlight, and foes who strike you from beside it take 1d6 radiant back). The chosen stars glimmer through your skin while you work.

As an action, speak a target's outstanding obligations aloud — real or symbolic. It makes a WIS save or is stunned for one round as the full weight of its debts, kept promises, and broken ones settles on it simultaneously.
Night itself takes your side: once per day, drown a battlefield in a darkness only you and your allies see through, for a whole scene.
Shattered bone orbits you in a grinding storm — 3d8 slashing each round to everything within 10ft, and arrows must find you through the whirl.

Transform into a beast you have seen, up to a CR limit that scales with level. You take on its stats; you revert at 0 HP or when you choose. Gear melds. Cannot cast spells while shaped until high level.

You and your companions become wisps of cloud — flying at tremendous speed (300ft), resistant to weapons, unable to act on the world. Reverting takes a full minute of stillness, and the whole party reverts together or not at all.
They were always there, waiting. Wings tear free when called and fold away to nothing — true flight, your own, in any armor, at any hour.
Kills plant life outright — crops blacken, vines slacken, a tree dies from the roots up. Plant creatures instead take 4d8 necrotic, CON for half.
Once per day, work a spell you do not know but have seen worked in your sight — friend's blessing or enemy's curse — once, exactly as it was done, at its normal cost.

Rumor of treasure finds you: word of every notable score — vaults, hoards, relics, shipments, hidden things — reaches your ears through fences, beggars, and thieves' talk. When you arrive somewhere new, the GM tells you what the local underworld knows is worth stealing, and roughly what stands in the way.

Your allies fight as though the battle were rehearsed: a glance repositions a companion, a nod springs the ambush, a raised fist holds the line. Whenever having a plan would matter, the party is treated as having one — even when there was no time to make it.
Your reputation does half the work now: the corrupt across a region know you are coming, and their servants must check their nerve or abandon them first.
Take the full shape of the dragon whose blood you carry — wings, breath, bulk and the fear that comes with it — for a scene. What you do wearing it is remembered.

Sanctify a 15ft-radius zone: each creature makes a CHA save on entering or starting its turn there; on a failure it cannot speak a deliberate lie while inside. You know whether each creature passed or failed. The compelled can still be evasive, answer selectively, or stay silent.
